title: There's no line here to end on Mac (replace the lone \\ with \vspace)
short_title: LaTeX says There's no line here to end? Use \vspace

runs.cmd: cd "$(mktemp -d)" && print -rl -- '\documentclass{article}' '\begin{document}' 'First paragraph.' '' '\\' 'Second paragraph.' '\end{document}' > main.tex && pdflatex -interaction=nonstopmode main.tex > out.txt; grep -m1 '^! LaTeX' out.txt; grep -n '^\\\\$' main.tex
runs.output:
! LaTeX Error: There's no line here to end.
5:\\

runs.cmd: cd "$(mktemp -d)" && print -rl -- '\documentclass{article}' '\begin{document}' 'First paragraph.' '' '\vspace{\baselineskip}' 'Second paragraph.' '\end{document}' > main.tex && pdflatex -interaction=nonstopmode main.tex > out.txt; grep -c '^\\\\$' main.tex; grep -c '^!' out.txt; grep 'Output written' out.txt
runs.output:
0
0
Output written on main.pdf (1 page, 14406 bytes).

verify.notes: Each run writes a small article in a fresh temporary folder and builds it once with pdfLaTeX from TeX Live 2026. With a double backslash alone on the line after a blank line, the build stops with There's no line here to end, because the blank line has already ended the paragraph and there is no line for the break to end. With that line replaced by \vspace{\baselineskip}, the same document builds with no errors. The TeX FAQ gives the same cause: \\ is a line break and LaTeX complains when it is not building a paragraph.

scenes.narration: Here is the error. Line five of the file is just a double backslash, placed after a blank line to add some space between two paragraphs.

scenes.text: A blank line already ends the paragraph. A double backslash only ends a line inside a paragraph, so after a blank line there is no line left for it to end.
scenes.narration: A blank line ends the paragraph. A double backslash is a line break, and it only works inside a paragraph. Placed after a blank line, there is no line for it to end, so LaTeX stops.
